operations.details: Current HMLR INSPIRE dataset page revalidated: polygons show position and indicative extent of registered freehold property.
HMLR explicitly states registered-title land extent cannot be established from INSPIRE Index Polygons alone; individual title plan is required.
Land Registry-INSPIRE ID is a unique identifier relating the polygon to a registered title.
One registered title may contain several separate polygons, each with its own Land Registry-INSPIRE ID.
Current download catalogue remains published 5 July 2026 with first-Sunday monthly refresh.
HMLR technical guidance revalidated: source geometry is captured against British National Grid.
HMLR warns BNG-to-WGS84 conversion may shift some features by up to 15m.
HMLR National Polygon technical specification revalidated: index polygons indicate registered-title location; title plan/register record general boundary position unless exact boundary determined.
Canonical height_difference_2 index currently displays labels including 'Exact HMLR poligonu' and describes native HMLR polygon workflow.
User-facing word 'Exact' is potentially ambiguous because it can be read as legal-boundary exactness rather than exact identifier/match semantics.
For this slot, 'exact' is locked to exact target row + exact HMLR INSPIRE ID + candidate point-inside matched geometry.
Exact HMLR ID match does not assert exact legal boundary, cadastral survey boundary, ownership extent or determined boundary.
Recommended display label: 'Exact HMLR ID eşleşmesi / gösterge niteliğinde INSPIRE poligonu'.
Recommended metric label: 'HMLR INSPIRE ID exact match; geometry indicative extent'.
Fail closed on labels such as 'exact legal parcel boundary', 'exact ownership boundary' or equivalent unsupported language.
EA DTM1m sampling continues over the matched HMLR INSPIRE geometry for reproducible measurement, with geometry semantics clearly disclosed.
Primary numeric metric remains EA DTM1m max-minus-min over valid pixel centres inside the matched geometry.
Terrain50 remains a secondary coarse crosscheck; HMLR label fix does not alter numeric values.
96% remains evidence/result confidence and is not a probability that HMLR geometry equals the legal boundary.
